question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Key territories exchanged or contested in the Anglo-Dutch Wars]
options: New Amsterdam (New York) — Ceded by the Dutch to the English under the Treaty of Breda (1667)
Run Island (Banda Islands) — English gave up this nutmeg island to the Dutch in the Treaty of Breda
Suriname — Remained a Dutch colony after the Anglo-Dutch Wars
Bombay — Captured by the Dutch from the English during the Second Anglo-Dutch War
wrong_fact: Bombay was never captured by the Dutch. Bombay was ceded by Portugal to England as part of the marriage dowry of Catherine of Braganza in 1661 and subsequently transferred by Charles II to the East India Company. The Dutch never held Bombay.
explanation: Under the Treaty of Breda (1667), the Dutch gave New Amsterdam (New York) to England in exchange for English claims to Run Island (Moluccas). Suriname continued as a Dutch colony. Bombay, however, came to England from Portugal — not from any Dutch capture — and the Dutch never controlled Bombay at any point.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Anglo-Dutch naval battles and their locations]
options: Battle of Medway (1667) — Dutch raid on the English fleet anchored in the River Medway, Kent
Battle of Solebay (1672) — Fought in the North Sea near Suffolk, England
Battle of Texel (1673) — Naval battle near the Dutch island of Texel in the North Sea
Battle of the Downs (1639) — English naval victory that decisively ended Dutch North Sea supremacy
wrong_fact: The Battle of the Downs (1639) was actually a Dutch victory over Spain (not England), where Dutch Admiral Tromp destroyed the Spanish fleet. It demonstrated Dutch naval power but was not an English victory nor did it end Dutch supremacy — quite the opposite, it confirmed Dutch dominance for a time.
explanation: The Battle of Medway (1667) was a famous Dutch audacity — attacking the English fleet in its home waters. Solebay (1672) and Texel (1673) were hard-fought Third Anglo-Dutch War battles. The Battle of the Downs (1639) was a Dutch-vs-Spanish engagement that showcased Dutch naval strength, not an English victory over the Dutch.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Impact of Anglo-Dutch Wars on trade routes and colonial possessions in Asia]
options: Strait of Malacca — Dutch retained control through the VOC after the Anglo-Dutch Wars, excluding English
Spice Islands (Moluccas) — Dutch monopoly reinforced after English were pushed out post-Amboyna Massacre (1623)
Coromandel Coast — Both Dutch and English competed for trade; Dutch had Nagapattinam as key port
Ceylon (Sri Lanka) — Jointly administered by the Dutch and English East India Companies after the Third Anglo-Dutch War
wrong_fact: Ceylon was never jointly administered by the Dutch and English. The Dutch captured Ceylon from the Portuguese between 1638–1658 and held it as a VOC possession exclusively. England only acquired Ceylon from the Dutch via the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814 (after the Napoleonic Wars), not after the 17th-century Anglo-Dutch Wars.
explanation: The Dutch held the Strait of Malacca, dominated the Moluccas after expelling the English (Amboyna Massacre 1623), and competed on the Coromandel Coast where Nagapattinam was their key port. Ceylon (Sri Lanka) was a fully Dutch possession from the 1650s–1796 and was never jointly administered with the English; England received it only in 1815 from the defeated Batavian Republic.
